- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.30) — model is overly conservative, missing downward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reaction to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns positive after a dip.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to overprediction in the immediate aftermath.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating upward momentum in early periods, then underestimating late-term volatility.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is rising > 0.20, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment is falling < -0.30, increase forecast by 5–10% to account for hidden support.
